payload.blocks: Phase 2 of plan 261124-0004-heads-operate-without-owner, and behind it phases 3, 6 and 7.
payload.headline: Phase 2 rerun: the request window drops --override, so the lead cannot pin claude-herdr-bypass-bwrap

parts.cause: The ticket's argv shows the request window forwarded run without --override and --timeout (earlier it also dropped --sync, --plan and --phase). The unit bound the default invocation, and its worker could not read the up-to-date brief in the main checkout because the p02 worktree is still on base f999c4018 and --sync is dropped too. Record: .fgos/assignments/unit-run-1795574308869-401c052f.

options.does: You paste one command (written in phase-02-argv-window.md, section Lead notes) from the main checkout: fgos run ... --sync main --override {executor claude, invocation claude-herdr-bypass-bwrap} --timeout 3h. Your shell is not behind the window, so every flag passes. The lead reads the result on its next wake, reviews and lands.
options.gain: Exactly the rerun you already approved; no config or code change; phase 2 moves today.
options.harm: Costs you one paste; the run takes up to 3 h of claude quota.
options.label: Owner runs the pinned rerun by hand

options.cost: One global config edit by you; lead rerun the same day.
options.does: Your earlier fallback: add --allowedTools Bash(cargo:*) Bash(node:*) Bash(npm test:*) to claude-cli-bwrap in the global ~/.fgos config, then the lead reruns through the window (still without --sync, so the brief would be passed inline).
options.gain: Lasting: every later claude unit can run cargo and node.
options.harm: Widens every claude worker on this machine, not just this rerun; the stale worktree base remains.
options.label: Global config patch for claude workers

options.cost: Unknown, a separate item (Rust head_request.rs or the Node branch); days.
options.does: A new backlog item makes the request window forward --override, --timeout, --sync, --plan and --phase of run; phase 2 waits for it.
options.gain: Removes the root cause for every lead.
options.harm: Phase 2 and the plan wait for another item; outside this plan's footprint.
options.label: Fix the window first

parts.recommendation: Owner runs the pinned rerun by hand: it is the run you already approved, with no lasting change; option 3 is worth a backlog row either way.

scope.allows: Option 1: you run that one command; the lead reviews and lands its result inside phase 2's footprint. Option 2: one global executor-args edit plus one rerun. Option 3: a backlog row and phase 2 parked on it.
scope.forbids: Any change to confinement policies, project executor args, worker git grants, other phases or the plan's scope.

parts.what: Per your answer to q-owq4jhwng7 I ran the phase 2 unit with --override {"executor":"claude","invocation":"claude-herdr-bypass-bwrap"} (ticket c-1632-1795574308428). It ended blocked after 19 s on the default claude-cli-bwrap invocation without touching a file, so the pinned rerun you allowed has not happened yet.
